newsitem.title: FINLAND: NESTE MUM ON OMV BOREALIS TALKS.
newsitem.headline: NESTE MUM ON OMV BOREALIS TALKS.

text.p: Finnish oil, chemicals and energy group Neste Oy on Thursday declined to say if it was holding talks with Austrian oil and chemicals group OMV AG on the sale of its stake in polyolefins group Borealis.
"We cannot confirm rumours like that," a Neste spokeswoman told Reuters by telephone.
An Austrian newspaper reported that OMV was negotiating to buy 50 percent of Borealis from Neste.
"We are still in talks with many parties on the sale of Borealis," the Neste spokeswoman said. "Nothing has changed," she added.
State-controlled Neste has said several times it is talking with various potential buyers on the sale of its half in petrochemicals firm Borealis, jointly owned with Norway's Statoil A/S.
The Austrian newspaper said the takeover would be engineered by OMV shareholder International Petroleum Investment Company (IPIC) and OMV.
Following the acquisition, OMV subsidiary Petrochemie Danubia (PCD) would be merged into Borealis, the paper said.
IPIC owns 19.6 percent of OMV, while Austrian state holding company OeIAG holds 35 percent.
OMV, Austria's largest industrial group, declined to comment on the report. OeIAG was unavailable for comment.
